result.title: CrossPanel: Exposing the Answer-Evidence Gap in Scientific Figure Understanding
result.summary: A correct answer to a scientific-figure question can conceal an incorrect account of the experiment. Reading evidence across panels requires keeping each observation attached to the object and conditions that give it meaning. We introduce CrossPanel, a benchmark of 2,650 human-reviewed questions that exposes this answer-evidence gap. Its tasks combine parallel observations or follow dependent queries, while a response audit separates object selection, experimental conditions, cross-panel binding, and local readout. Across 15 vision-language models on 251 diagnostic questions, 8.42%-56.64% of correct answers contain explicit factual errors. The audit distinguishes coherent readings of the wrong target from incorrect readings of the right one. Controlled interventions then test how these failures can be repaired: verified object-condition hints, which withhold the requested measurement, raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's target-query success by 22.81 percentage points on 57 questions, while additional image tiles alone yield little improvement. Other models benefit most from combining both forms of assistance. These findings identify experimental attribution as a distinct requirement alongside local perception, and make both measurable beyond final-answer accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CrossPanel 基准（2,650 道人工审校问题），通过跨面板绑定与依赖追问暴露科学图表理解中的「答案—证据」缺口，并用响应审计把对象选择、实验条件、跨面板绑定和局部读数分开，再以提示干预检验失败能否修复。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心正是视觉证据是否被正确绑定并真正用于答案，对「答案是否正确但依据错误」这一贡献分配与证据筛选问题提供了可核查的诊断范式和干预结果，与 LVR 中视觉细节保留和证据使用评价直接相关。
